newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees stable end 1996/97 grain intvn stocks.
newsitem.headline: EU sees stable end 1996/97 grain intvn stocks.

text.p: European Union grain supply and demand is likely to be balanced at the end of 1996/97 (July/June) with little change in intervention stocks, a Commission grain official said.
The official noted at a recent meeting of the EU's cereals advisory committee that the grain balance sheets of the Commission and Coceral both foresaw equilibrium.
"As a result, intervention will be very limited and will probably not exceed 3.0 million tonnes," Coceral minutes of the meeting quoted the official as saying.
Intervention grain stocks totalled 2.6 million tonnes at the start of 1996/97.
The Commission put the 1996 grain harvest at 201 million tonnes, against 203 million by Coceral. It put consumption at 170 million tonnes, against 172 million by Coceral.
EU grain export commitments totalled 26.5 million tonnes to April 22, compared with a Coceral forecast of 27.6 million tonnes for the full season.
Coceral put overall private and public grain stocks at 31.1 million tonnes at the end of 1996/97.

A key feature this season was a six to seven million tonnes increase in cereals consumption due to the large EU harvest of feed cereals and decline in soybean imports due to high prices, according to a Coceral official.

Noting that intervention stocks would be little changed in 1996/97 and given uncertainty over the 1997 crop, the official argued that the set-aside rate should stay at five percent for the 1998 harvest.
